data.description:
## What / Why

The mutation-append and churn-append subcommands use a read-check-post pattern for idempotency: read ticket comments, grep for HTML marker, post if absent. Two concurrent invocations for the same (pr, kind) pair can both pass the marker-absent check before either posts, resulting in duplicate entries. This is a TOCTOU race condition.

Wrap the read-check-post sequence in flock (or equivalent atomic primitive) scoped per (pr, kind) tuple so concurrent invocations are serialized.

## Files to Modify / Create

- plugins/dso/scripts/calibration-report.sh — add flock wrapper around the read-check-post block in both mutation-append and churn-append; lock file path: /tmp/calibration-rollup-<kind>-<pr>.lock; use flock -xn or flock -x with timeout; release lock on exit (trap ERR EXIT)
- tests/scripts/test-calibration-concurrent-append.sh — AMEND (task 394e): Scenario B (same PR twice) must now pass deterministically because flock serializes the duplicate; assert exactly 1 ticket-comment call without relying on stub timing

## Story DD Coverage

- dd-5 (partial): idempotency guard is race-safe (amends the behavioral guarantee stated in dd-5)

## Given / When / Then (test approach)

Given two background subshells running mutation-append --pr=101 simultaneously
When flock is in place
Then second invocation blocks until first completes; exactly 1 comment posted

Given flock lock files
When append completes or fails
Then lock file released (trap-based cleanup)

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: flock wraps read-check-post in both mutation-append and churn-append; lock file scoped to (kind, pr) tuple
- AC2: Lock file cleaned up via trap ERR EXIT even on error
- AC3: Concurrent test (394e Scenario B: same PR twice) passes deterministically — not flaky
- AC4: flock timeout specified (e.g., 10s) so stuck locks do not hang CI indefinitely

## Testing Mode

RED — flock guard does not yet exist

## Retry Budget

2
data.title: Add filesystem-level flock guard to calibration-report.sh append subcommands for TOCTOU safety
